mainTopic: How offerings are arranged and waved in תנופה, what the waving means, and how communal שלמים are waved after שחיטה
overview: The גמרא explains how the כהן stacks the pieces of a קרבן for תנופה: the אימורין on the palm, the חזה ושוק on top of them, and any bread on the very top, as at the מלואים. Two פסוקים seem to put the fat on top. The גמרא explains that they describe the carrying from the slaughter area and the handoff to the burning כהן, since the pieces flip at each handoff. From this it learns that three כהנים do the job, because בְּרׇב עָם הַדְרַת מֶלֶךְ. Next comes a ברייתא about waving the שתי הלחם with the two lambs of עצרת. It gives four views: bread on top, lambs on top, loaves between the lambs' thighs, and רבי's side by side, since for him 'על' can mean 'next to.' רבי יוחנן and the sages of ארץ ישראל explain the meaning of the waving motions, and we learn that even שירי מצוה hold back calamity, including the waving of the לולב. Finally, a ברייתא records a מחלוקת between רבי and חכמים over whether communal שלמים are waved whole or only the חזה ושוק after שחיטה. The גמרא explains it as an argument over דון מינה ומינה versus דון מינה ואוקי באתרה.

steps.title: How the pieces are stacked for waving
steps.stepSummary: For תנופה, the אימורין go on the palm, the חזה ושוק go on top of them, and any bread goes on the very top.
steps.simpleTranslation: How is it done? He places the fats on the palm of the hand, and the breast and thigh on top of them. Whenever bread comes with the offering, the bread goes on top.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא lays out the order of the pieces stacked on the hand for תנופה. The order is fats on the bottom, then the חזה ושוק, then any bread on top.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This sets a three-layer order. The next steps ask where each part of this order comes from: first the bread on top, then the fats under the חזה ושוק.

keyTerms.meaning: The parts of a קרבן that are burned on the מזבח, mainly the fats
The palm of the hand
The breast and thigh, the portions given to the כהן
Bread or loaves brought together with certain קרבנות

steps.whatToRemember: Order on the hand, from bottom to top: אימורין, then חזה ושוק, then bread.

phrases.english: How does he do it?
He places the sacrificial fats on the palm of the hand,
and the breast and thigh on top of them,
and in any case where there is bread,
the bread is on top.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: For תנופה the order is אימורין on the bottom, חזה ושוק above them, and bread on top.

steps.title: Where do we see bread on top?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where we find that the bread goes on top.
steps.simpleTranslation: Where?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for a source for the last rule, that bread goes on top. This sets up רב פפא's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule about bread is stated broadly ('any place where there is bread'). So the גמרא wants to know which case in the תורה actually shows this order.

keyTerms.meaning: Where? Asking for the case or source
On top, above

phrases.english: Where?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the bread-on-top rule from step 1
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which case shows that the bread is placed on top during תנופה

steps.title: The inauguration shows the bread on top
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא answers that the source is the מלואים, where the bread was placed on the fats and the thigh.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: at the inauguration of the כהנים.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא answers the question: the source is the מלואים, the inauguration of the כהנים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At the מלואים the פסוק says משה placed the loaves 'on the fats and on the right thigh.' That shows the bread sits above everything else.

keyTerms.meaning: The seven-day inauguration of אהרן and his sons as כהנים

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said: At the inauguration.
phrases.notes: ויקרא 8:26. There the loaves were placed on top of the fats and the right thigh.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 2
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The מלואים, where the bread was placed on the fats and the thigh

steps.title: What is the source that the fats go underneath?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source that the אימורין go below the חזה ושוק. It suggests a פסוק that says the חזה ושוק are brought 'on' the fats.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason? If you say it is because it is written: 'The thigh of heaving and the breast of waving they shall bring on the fire-offerings of the fats, to wave as a waving'...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks where we learn that the fats go on the bottom. It offers a possible source, but the word אילימא tells us a challenge is about to come.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proposed פסוק says the חזה ושוק are brought 'on' (על) the fats. That would put the fats underneath, which fits the rule in step 1.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason or source?
If you say. It offers a suggestion that is about to be challenged
Waving the offering back and forth before ה'
The fats that are burned on the fire of the מזבח

phrases.english: What is the reason?
If you say it is because it is written:
"The thigh of heaving and the breast of waving
phrases.notes: ויקרא 10:15

phrases.english: on the fire-offerings of the fats
they shall bring, to wave as a waving",

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from the bread rule to the rule that the fats go under the חזה ושוק
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source that the אימורין go below the חזה ושוק

steps.title: Another verse puts the fat on top
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the suggestion: another פסוק says the fat is brought 'on' the חזה, which is the opposite order.
steps.simpleTranslation: But isn't it written: 'The fat on the breast he shall bring'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points to a different פסוק that seems to put the fat on top of the חזה. That contradicts the first פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each פסוק uses the word 'על' (on), but they point in opposite directions. So the first פסוק cannot simply prove the order unless we explain the second one.

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it written? It introduces a contradicting פסוק
Fat, the part burned on the מזבח

phrases.english: But isn't it written:
"The fat on the breast he shall bring"!
phrases.notes: ויקרא 7:30

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָכְתִיב: אֶת הַחֵלֶב עַל הֶחָזֶה יְבִיאֶנּוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the proposed source from step 4
steps.kashyaTarget: Using ויקרא 10:15 as proof that the fats go underneath
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: ויקרא 7:30 says the fat is on the חזה, which is the reverse order, so the פסוקים seem to contradict each other

steps.title: The second verse describes carrying, not waving
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains that the second פסוק describes how the כהן carries the pieces from the slaughter area. When he flips them onto the waving כהן's hand, the fat ends up on the bottom.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: That verse is about when a כהן brings it from the slaughtering area, and then he turns it over.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי resolves the contradiction. Each פסוק describes a different moment in the process.
steps.deeperAnalysis: While carrying the pieces, the כהן holds the fat on top of the חזה. He then turns them over onto the hand of the כהן who waves, so the order flips and the fat ends up underneath. Both פסוקים are true, and during the waving itself the fats are on the bottom.

keyTerms.meaning: The slaughtering area in the עזרה
Throws or places. Here it means turns over onto the other hand

steps.whatToRemember: While carrying, the fat is on top. The כהן then flips the pieces, so while waving the fat is on the bottom, under the חזה ושוק.
steps.confusionAlert: Both פסוקים are correct. Each one describes a different stage, carrying versus waving, so they do not argue about the waving order.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
That verse is when a priest brings it
phrases.notes: He means the second פסוק, 'the fat on the breast.'

phrases.english: from the slaughtering area,
and he turns it over.
phrases.notes: He flips it onto the hand of the כהן who waves, so the fat that was on top ends up on the bottom.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: הָהוּא דְּמַיְיתֵי לֵיהּ כֹּהֵן מִבֵּית הַמִּטְבָּחַיִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 5
steps.terutzResolutionType: Each פסוק refers to a different stage of the process
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two פסוקים seem to give opposite orders for the waving
steps.terutzMaskana: ויקרא 7:30 describes carrying from the slaughter area. After the pieces are flipped, the fats are on the bottom for the waving, as ויקרא 10:15 says

steps.title: Another verse puts the fats on top of the breasts
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the rule that the fats go under the breast and thigh. It cites a פסוק that says the fats were placed on the breasts.
steps.simpleTranslation: But doesn't a פסוק say: 'And they put the fats upon the breasts'? That sounds like the fats are on top.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises another פסוק that seems to say the fats go on top of the breasts. That is the opposite of what we have been trying to prove.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי already explained one פסוק that put the fat on top: it described carrying the pieces from the slaughter area. This is a different פסוק, about the actual service, and it also puts the חלבים on the חזות. So the question is how this second picture of fat-on-top fits.

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it written? (opens a challenge from a פסוק)
The fats of the offering that are burned on the מזבח (the אימורין)
Breasts (plural of חָזֶה), the breast portions given to the כהן

phrases.english: But isn't it written:
"And they put the fats upon the breasts"?
phrases.notes: ויקרא 9:20

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second challenge from a different פסוק, after אביי resolved the first one.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the אימורין go below the חזה ושוק during waving.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A פסוק explicitly describes the fats being placed on the breasts. That suggests the fats are on top.

steps.title: That verse describes the handoff to the burning כהן
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק describes when the waving כהן passes the parts to a different כהן, who goes and burns them. The flip in that handoff puts the fats back on top.
steps.simpleTranslation: That פסוק is talking about when he gives the parts to another כהן, who then goes and burns them on the מזבח.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the second פסוק describes a later stage, after the waving. The parts are handed to another כהן to burn.
steps.deeperAnalysis: It works the same way as אביי's answer. Each time the pieces are passed from hand to hand they get turned over. So after waving, the fats end up on top again, which is the order this פסוק describes.

keyTerms.meaning: Another כהן (here, the one who burns the parts)
Burns (on the מזבח)
The burning of sacrificial parts on the מזבח

phrases.english: That is when he gives it to another כהן,
phrases.notes: The waving כהן hands the pieces over, and they flip again, so now the fats are on top.

phrases.english: and he goes and burns it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Different stage: the פסוק describes a later moment in the process, not the waving itself.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק shows that during waving the fats lie on top of the breasts.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק describes the handoff to the burning כהן. During the waving itself, the fats are underneath.

steps.title: The service needs three כהנים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא learns from this that three כהנים are used: one carries, one waves, one burns. The source is 'In the multitude of people is the King's glory.'
steps.simpleTranslation: This teaches us that we need three כהנים, because it is written: 'In the multitude of people is the King's glory.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws a new rule from the answer it just gave. The job is split among three כהנים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two answers show three different hands: the one who brings the parts, the one who waves, and the one who burns. One כהן could do it all. Spreading it among more כהנים gives more honor to ה׳, as the פסוק in משלי says.

keyTerms.meaning: It teaches us (a new point)
Three כהנים
In the multitude of people is the King's glory

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the classic source for doing a מצוה with many people, so that ה׳ gets more honor.
steps.whatToRemember: The pieces flip with each handoff. Fats are on top when carried in, on the bottom during waving, and on top again for burning. Three כהנים do the job because of בְּרׇב עָם הַדְרַת מֶלֶךְ.

phrases.english: And this teaches us
that we require three כהנים,
because it is written:
"In the multitude of people is the King's glory."
phrases.notes: משלי 14:28

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a practical rule out of the two answers in Steps 6 and 8.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The carrying, waving and burning are done by three separate כהנים, because בְּרׇב עָם הַדְרַת מֶלֶךְ.

steps.title: Back to the משנה: waving the two loaves and two lambs
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about the שתי הלחם and the two lambs of עצרת. It brings a ברייתא on the פסוק about waving them.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: the two loaves and the two lambs of עצרת need waving. The רבנן taught: 'And the כהן shall wave them upon the bread of the first fruits.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next case in the משנה, the עצרת offering. It sets up a ברייתא that will ask how the bread and lambs are arranged for waving.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here there are two kinds of items, bread and lambs, waved together. The ברייתא starts from the words 'upon the bread of the first fruits,' which seem to say the lambs sit on top of the bread.

keyTerms.meaning: The two loaves brought on שבועות
The two lambs (שלמים) brought with them on עצרת, which is שבועות
And he shall wave (from תְּנוּפָה)
Bread of the first fruits, the two loaves

phrases.english: And the two loaves and the two lambs of עצרת, etc.
The Rabbis taught:
"And the כהן shall wave them
upon the bread of the first fruits,"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 23:20

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the topic of fats and breasts and returns to the next line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The two loaves and the two lambs of עצרת are waved together, based on ויקרא 23:20.

steps.title: Not lambs on top of the bread
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא suggests the lambs might be placed on the bread. It rejects that, because the פסוק also says 'upon the two lambs.'
steps.simpleTranslation: You might think he should put the lambs on top of the bread. That is why the פסוק says 'upon the two lambs.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא raises a possible reading, that the lambs go on top. It knocks it down with other words in the same פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Upon the bread' sounds like lambs on top of bread. But the same פסוק also says 'upon the two lambs,' which sounds like bread on top of lambs. So the first reading cannot be the whole story.

keyTerms.meaning: One might think (introduces a possible reading that will be rejected)
The פסוק teaches (shows from the text why that reading is wrong)
On top of

phrases.aramaic: יָכוֹל יַנִּיחַ כְּבָשִׂים עַל גַּבֵּי הַלֶּחֶם?
phrases.english: One might think he should place the lambs on top of the bread?
The verse states: "upon the two lambs."
phrases.notes: The same פסוק, ויקרא 23:20, also has these words, which point the other way: bread on the lambs.

steps.triggerLanguage: יָכוֹל יַנִּיחַ כְּבָשִׂים עַל גַּבֵּי הַלֶּחֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests a reading of the פסוק quoted in Step 10.
steps.raayaObject: The lambs are not placed on top of the bread.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The words 'עַל שְׁנֵי כְּבָשִׂים' in ויקרא 23:20.

steps.title: Not bread on top of the lambs either
steps.stepSummary: If we follow 'upon the two lambs,' the bread would go on top. But that is rejected too, because the פסוק says 'upon the bread of the first fruits.'
steps.simpleTranslation: If you go by 'upon the two lambs,' you might think the bread goes on top of the lambs. That is why the פסוק says 'upon the bread of the first fruits.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא turns the argument around and rules out the opposite order as well. Each half of the פסוק cancels the other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now both orders have been rejected: neither lambs on bread nor bread on lambs. That leaves the question of how they are actually held, which the ברייתא answers in its next line.

keyTerms.meaning: If (we go by this reading)
Lambs

steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא is not contradicting itself. It is using each half of the פסוק to rule out the other order, so that the פסוק by itself cannot decide which one goes on top. The ברייתא then settles it: the bread goes on top.

phrases.english: If it is "upon the two lambs,"
one might think the bread goes on top of the lambs?
The verse states: "upon the bread of the first fruits."

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי ״עַל שְׁנֵי כְּבָשִׂים״ יָכוֹל לֶחֶם עַל גַּבֵּי כְּבָשִׂים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Mirrors Step 11 in the other direction.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that the bread is placed on top of the lambs.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The words 'upon the bread of the first fruits' imply the lambs are on the bread. So the bread cannot simply be on top.

steps.title: The verse is evenly balanced
steps.stepSummary: Since each phrase of the פסוק cancels the other, the ברייתא says it cannot tell whether the bread or the lambs go on top.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse is balanced. I do not know whether the bread goes on top of the lambs or the lambs on top of the bread.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא sums up steps 11 and 12. The two phrases of the פסוק point in opposite directions, so we are stuck. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 11 ruled out lambs on top because of 'upon the two lambs.' Step 12 ruled out bread on top because of 'upon the bread of the first fruits.' Each option is supported by one phrase and knocked out by the other, so the פסוק alone cannot decide.

keyTerms.meaning: The verse is evenly balanced. It can be read both ways equally.
On top of.
Lambs. Here, the two שלמים lambs of עצרת.

phrases.english: The verse is evenly balanced,
and I do not know
whether the bread is on top of the lambs,
or the lambs are on top of the bread.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sums up the deadlock created by steps 11 and 12.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which goes on top during the waving: the bread or the lambs?

steps.title: Bread goes on top, as it does everywhere else
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא breaks the deadlock by comparing to other wavings, where the bread is always on top.
steps.simpleTranslation: Just as everywhere else the bread is on top, so too here the bread is on top.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers its own question. It looks at how waving is done elsewhere and copies that pattern.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק itself is stuck, so the ברייתא uses a general pattern found in other cases. Wherever bread and meat are waved together, the bread is on top. So here too the bread goes on top of the lambs.

keyTerms.meaning: Just as we find. A comparison to a known case.
Above, on top.
So too here.

phrases.aramaic: מָה מָצִינוּ בְּכׇל מָקוֹם – לֶחֶם לְמַעְלָה,
phrases.english: Just as we find everywhere – the bread is above,
so too here, the bread is above.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question raised in step 13.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Bread goes on top, following the pattern found in other wavings.

steps.title: Where do we find bread on top?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pauses the ברייתא to ask where this 'everywhere' pattern actually appears.
steps.simpleTranslation: Where is this found?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא steps out of the ברייתא for a moment. It asks for the source of the claim that bread is always on top. The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא said 'everywhere' but did not name a case. The גמרא wants a real case where a פסוק places bread above meat.

keyTerms.meaning: Where?

phrases.english: Where?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source behind step 14's comparison.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which case shows bread placed above during waving?

steps.title: רב פפא: at the מילואים
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא answers that the pattern is found at the inauguration offering of the כהנים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא says: at the מילואים.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא names the source: the מילואים, the offerings brought when the כהנים were first inaugurated.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At the מילואים the bread was placed on top of the fats and the thigh. That gives a real case behind the ברייתא's word 'everywhere.'

keyTerms.meaning: The inauguration offerings of אהרן and his sons.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa says:
At the inauguration.
phrases.notes: ויקרא 8:26–27, where the loaves were placed on the fats and the thigh.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 15.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The מילואים, where bread was placed above the meat.

steps.title: רבי יוסי בן המשולם: the lambs go on top
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי בן המשולם puts the lambs on top. He reads 'upon the two lambs' as teaching that only two lambs are waved, not the seven.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי בן המשולם says: the lambs go on top. What then do I do with 'upon the two lambs'? It comes to exclude the seven.
steps.whatsHappening: Back in the ברייתא, a second opinion disagrees. It puts the lambs on top and explains the phrase that seemed to argue against him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Upon the two lambs' seemed to require bread on top. רבי יוסי בן המשולם says the phrase is not about placement at all. It tells us that only the two שלמים lambs are waved with the bread, not the seven עולה lambs.

keyTerms.meaning: And how do I explain? A way of reading a phrase that seems to argue against you.
To exclude.
Seven. The seven עולה lambs of עצרת.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei ben HaMeshullam says:
The lambs are above,
and how do I explain 'upon the two lambs'?
It comes to exclude the seven.
phrases.notes: These are the seven lambs brought as עולות on עצרת (ויקרא 23:18). They are not waved with the bread.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with step 14, which put the bread on top.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The lambs go on top. 'Upon the two lambs' limits the waving to the two lambs and leaves out the seven.

steps.title: חנינא בן חכינאי: loaves between the lambs' thighs
steps.stepSummary: חנינא בן חכינאי puts the loaves between the lambs' thighs, so that both verses are kept at once.
steps.simpleTranslation: חנינא בן חכינאי says: he places the two loaves between the thighs of the lambs and waves them. That keeps both verses: bread on top of lambs, and lambs on top of bread.
steps.whatsHappening: A third opinion tries to satisfy both phrases of the פסוק together, using a physical arrangement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the loaves are tucked between the lambs' thighs, part of the bread is above lamb and part of a lamb is above bread. So both 'upon' phrases are true at the same time.

keyTerms.meaning: Their thighs.
Waves (does the תנופה).
Two verses, here the two phrases of the פסוק.

phrases.english: Chanina ben Chachinai says:
He places the two loaves
between the thighs of the lambs and waves,
and it turns out he keeps both of these verses:
bread on top of lambs,
and lambs on top of the bread.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third view that tries to keep both phrases of the פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The loaves go between the lambs' thighs, which keeps both verses.

steps.title: רבי: that would be disrespectful before הקב״ה
steps.stepSummary: רבי rejects חנינא בן חכינאי's arrangement. Nobody would serve a human king that way, so certainly not הקב״ה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי said: before a flesh-and-blood king one would not do this. Should one do it before the King of kings, הקב״ה?!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי attacks the thighs arrangement on grounds of respect.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The objection is not about the wording of the פסוק but about honor. Bread pressed between animal thighs would not be presented to a human king, so it cannot be the right way to serve הקב״ה.

keyTerms.meaning: A flesh-and-blood king, meaning a human king.
The King of kings, meaning הקב״ה.

phrases.english: Rabbi said:

phrases.aramaic: לִפְנֵי מֶלֶךְ בָּשָׂר וְדָם אֵין עוֹשִׂין כֵּן,
phrases.english: Before a flesh-and-blood king one does not do this,
before the King of kings of kings,
the Holy One, Blessed be He, should one do this?!

steps.triggerLanguage: לִפְנֵי מֶלֶךְ בָּשָׂר וְדָם אֵין עוֹשִׂין כֵּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects step 18.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: חנינא בן חכינאי's arrangement of loaves between the thighs.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It is disrespectful, something you would not even do before a human king.

steps.title: רבי: place them side by side and wave
steps.stepSummary: רבי's own view is that the loaves and lambs are placed next to each other and waved together.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, he places them one next to the other and waves.
steps.whatsHappening: After rejecting the thighs arrangement, רבי gives his own method: side by side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רבי's method nothing is on top of anything. The bread and lambs lie next to each other and are waved together, which is respectful.

keyTerms.meaning: One beside the other.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא מַנִּיחַ זֶה בְּצַד זֶה וּמֵנִיף.
phrases.english: Rather, he places one beside the other and waves.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא מַנִּיחַ זֶה בְּצַד זֶה וּמֵנִיף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבי's positive ruling after rejecting step 18.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The loaves and lambs are placed side by side and waved.

steps.title: But the פסוק says 'upon'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי: side by side does not fit the word 'על' (upon).
steps.simpleTranslation: But we need 'upon'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי's side-by-side method using the wording of the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says one thing is 'upon' the other. Side by side seems to ignore that word completely.

keyTerms.meaning: But don't we need? An opening for a challenge.
Upon. It can also mean 'next to.'

phrases.english: But we require 'upon'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי's ruling in step 20.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The word 'על' seems to require one item on top of the other, and side by side does not do that.

steps.title: For רבי, 'על' means 'next to'
steps.stepSummary: רבי holds elsewhere too that 'על' can mean next to, so side by side keeps the פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said to רב המנונא (some say רב המנונא to רב חסדא): רבי follows his own reasoning, since he says 'על' means 'next to.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge: רבי reads 'על' as 'beside,' just as he does in other places.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge assumed 'על' must mean 'on top of.' The answer is that רבי consistently reads 'על' as 'next to.' So placing the bread beside the lambs fully keeps the פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: Following his own reasoning, matching his view elsewhere.
Next to, adjacent.

steps.whatToRemember: There are four views on the waving. The ברייתא's first view puts bread on top, as at the מילואים. רבי יוסי בן המשולם puts the lambs on top. חנינא בן חכינאי puts the loaves between the thighs. רבי puts them side by side, because for him 'על' means 'next to.'
steps.confusionAlert: רבי is not ignoring the word 'על.' He reads it in a different way, as 'beside' rather than 'on top of.'

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב חִסְדָּא לְרַב הַמְנוּנָא,
phrases.english: Rav Chisda said to Rav Hamnuna,

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמְרִי לַהּ רַב הַמְנוּנָא לְרַב חִסְדָּא:
phrases.english: and some say Rav Hamnuna said it to Rav Chisda:
Rabbi follows his own reasoning,
for he says 'upon' means next to.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 21.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereads the key word, based on the sage's view elsewhere.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'על' must mean on top of, so side by side breaks the פסוק.
steps.terutzMaskana: For רבי, 'על' means next to, so side by side keeps the פסוק.

steps.title: Proof that רבי reads 'upon' as 'next to'
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows that רבי reads 'על' as 'next to' in the פסוק about the לחם הפנים. His proof is the פסוק about the פרוכת and the ארון.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: 'And you shall put pure frankincense upon (על) the row.' רבי says 'על' here means next to. Do you say it means next to, or maybe it really means on top? Since the תורה says 'and you shall screen על the ארון with the פרוכת', you must say 'על' means next to.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source for the claim in the last step that רבי reads 'על' as 'next to'. It quotes a ברייתא where he says exactly that.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the ברייתא, רבי explains that the frankincense is placed beside the rows of bread, not on top of them. He proves that 'על' can mean 'next to' from the פרוכת, which hung beside the ארון and not on top of it. So reading 'על' as 'next to' is a consistent way רבי reads פסוקים, and it backs up his side-by-side placement of the loaves and lambs.

keyTerms.meaning: Next to, close by
Actually, literally
A row (here, a row of the לחם הפנים)
The curtain in front of the קודש הקדשים
You must therefore say (it is proven)

steps.whatToRemember: For רבי, 'על' can mean 'next to'. So placing the loaves beside the lambs still fits the פסוק.

phrases.english: As it is taught: 'And you shall put pure frankincense upon the row,'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 24:7, about the לחם הפנים.

phrases.english: Rabbi says: 'upon' means next to.
Do you say 'upon' means next to,
or does it mean only actually on top?

phrases.aramaic: כְּשֶׁהוּא אוֹמֵר ״וְסַכֹּתָ עַל הָאָרֹן אֶת הַפָּרֹכֶת״,
phrases.english: When it says, 'And you shall screen upon the Ark with the curtain,'
phrases.notes: שמות 40:3. The פרוכת hung beside the ארון, not on top of it.

phrases.english: you must say 'upon' means next to.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source for step 22's claim about how רבי reads 'על'.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that רבי reads 'על' as 'next to'
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא on ויקרא 24:7, proven from שמות 40:3 (the פרוכת beside the ארון)

steps.title: Why the waving goes in all directions and up and down
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's description of the waving. רבי יוחנן explains that the waving honors הקב״ה, Who owns all directions, heaven and earth.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: 'He moves them out and back, up and down.' רבי חייא בר אבא said in the name of רבי יוחנן: out and back is for the One Who owns the directions. Up and down is for the One Who owns heaven and earth.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new piece of the משנה: how the waving is done. It gives רבי יוחנן's reason for the two kinds of motion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה describes two motions: out and back toward each direction, and up and down. רבי יוחנן gives each motion a meaning. The sideways motion dedicates the offering to the Owner of all directions, and the vertical motion dedicates it to the Owner of heaven and earth.

keyTerms.meaning: Moves out and brings back (toward each direction)
Raises and lowers
Directions (here, the four directions of the world)

phrases.english: He extends and brings back, raises and lowers, etc.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא, אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba said that Rabbi Yochanan said:
He extends and brings back for the One to Whom the directions belong;

phrases.aramaic: מַעֲלֶה וּמוֹרִיד – לְמִי שֶׁהַשָּׁמַיִם וְהָאָרֶץ שֶׁלּוֹ.
phrases.english: he raises and lowers for the One to Whom heaven and earth belong.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the 'על' discussion and starts explaining the waving described in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The waving dedicates the offering to הקב״ה, Owner of all directions, heaven and earth.

steps.title: The version from ארץ ישראל: the waving holds back harmful winds and dews
steps.stepSummary: In ארץ ישראל they taught a different reason: the waving holds back harmful winds and harmful dews.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the West they taught it this way. רב חמא בר עוקבא said in the name of רבי יוסי בר רבי חנינא: out and back is to hold back harmful winds. Up and down is to hold back harmful dews.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second version of the explanation, as it was taught in ארץ ישראל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן's version was about honoring הקב״ה. This version is about protection. The sideways motion stops harmful winds that come from every direction, and the vertical motion stops harmful dews that come from above.

keyTerms.meaning: In the West, meaning ארץ ישראל
To hold back, to stop
Harmful winds
Harmful dews

phrases.english: In the West they taught it like this:
phrases.notes: 'The West' means ארץ ישראל, which is west of בבל.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב חָמָא בַּר עוּקְבָא, אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר רַבִּי חֲנִינָא:
phrases.english: Rav Chama bar Ukva said that Rabbi Yosei bar Rabbi Chanina said:

phrases.aramaic: מוֹלִיךְ וּמֵבִיא – כְּדֵי לַעֲצוֹר רוּחוֹת רָעוֹת,
phrases.english: He extends and brings back in order to hold back harmful winds;

phrases.aramaic: מַעֲלֶה וּמוֹרִיד – כְּדֵי לַעֲצוֹר טְלָלִים רָעִים.
phrases.english: he raises and lowers in order to hold back harmful dews.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different version of step 24's explanation, as taught in ארץ ישראל.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The waving motions hold back harmful winds and harmful dews.

steps.title: Even the extra parts of a מצוה hold back calamity
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי בר רב אבין learns from the ארץ ישראל version that שירי מצוה, the non-essential parts of a מצוה, hold back calamity.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי בר רב אבין said: This shows that the leftover parts of a מצוה hold back calamity. Waving is a leftover part of a מצוה, and yet it holds back harmful winds and harmful dews.
steps.whatsHappening: An אמורא draws a general lesson from the explanation in the previous step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: תנופה is only a שירי מצוה: if it was left out, the offering still counts. Even so, the previous step said it holds back harmful winds and dews. So even the 'extra' parts of a מצוה have great power to protect.

keyTerms.meaning: This shows, we can learn from here
The leftover, non-essential parts of a מצוה
Calamity, punishment
Waving of an offering

steps.whatToRemember: Even a part of a מצוה that is not required to fulfill it, like the תנופה, protects against calamity.
steps.confusionAlert: שירי מצוה does not mean an unimportant act. It only means you have still fulfilled the מצוה if you skipped it. The point here is that even such a part is very powerful.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר רַב אָבִין:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei bar Rav Avin said:

phrases.aramaic: זֹאת אוֹמֶרֶת שְׁיָרֵי מִצְוָה מְעַכְּבִים אֶת הַפּוּרְעָנוּת,
phrases.english: This shows that the leftover parts of a מצוה hold back calamity,
for waving is a leftover part of a מצוה,
phrases.notes: He means the offering still counts even if the waving was not done.

phrases.english: and yet it holds back harmful winds and harmful dews.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a general principle from step 25's explanation.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שירי מצוה hold back calamity, as we see from the תנופה.

steps.title: The same applies to the לולב
steps.stepSummary: רבה adds that the same idea applies to waving the לולב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: And the same is true of a לולב.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה takes the lesson about the waving in the בית המקדש and applies it to the לולב on סוכות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The לולב is also waved out and back and up and down. So the same meaning, and the same power to hold back harmful winds and dews, applies to the לולב too.

keyTerms.meaning: And the same is true
The palm branch waved on סוכות

steps.whyThisMatters: This links the waving of the לולב to the waving of the offerings, which gives the motions of the לולב the same meaning.

phrases.english: Rabbah said: And so too with a lulav.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the waving discussion to the לולב.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The לולב is waved in the same manner and for the same reasons.

steps.title: רב אחא's arrow in the eye of the שטן
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בר יעקב would wave his לולב out and back and say, 'An arrow in the eye of the שטן.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא בר יעקב would move the לולב outward and bring it back, showing how it is done, and he would say: 'An arrow in the eye of the שטן!'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a short story about how רב אחא בר יעקב waved his לולב and what he said while doing it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This follows straight from רבה's point that waving the לולב also holds back harm. רב אחא treated each wave as a blow against the שטן, the force that brings harm and pushes people to sin.

keyTerms.meaning: Moves it outward and brings it back, the back-and-forth motion of waving
An arrow
The שטן, the force that accuses people and brings harm

phrases.english: Rav Acha bar Yaakov
would move it outward and bring it back,
and would show it like this,
and would say: 'An arrow in the eye of the Satan.'

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אַחָא בַּר יַעֲקֹב מַמְטֵי לֵיהּ וּמַיְיתֵי לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows a sage acting on רבה's idea that waving the לולב holds back harm.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב אחא בר יעקב waved the לולב and declared it an arrow in the שטן's eye.

steps.title: Saying this is unwise because it provokes the שטן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says רב אחא's statement was not proper, because it invites the שטן to fight back.
steps.simpleTranslation: But this is not a proper thing to say, because the שטן will come and be provoked by it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא disagrees with what רב אחא used to say. It explains that taunting the שטן is a mistake.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא does not reject the waving itself, only the boastful words. Openly challenging the שטן can stir him up to attack harder.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not a proper thing (to do or say)
To be provoked, to start up a fight

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying that waving the לולב is wrong. Only the taunting phrase 'an arrow in the eye of the שטן' is criticized.

phrases.english: But it is not a proper thing,
because he will come to be provoked by it.
phrases.notes: 'He' is the שטן. Taunting him may push him to try harder to make people sin.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the wording רב אחא used in the story just told.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only רב אחא's declaration, not the act of waving.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Taunting the שטן provokes him to strike back.

steps.title: How the communal peace offerings are waved after slaughter
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא: the communal שלמים are waved after שחיטה. רבי says the whole animal is waved, and חכמים say only the breast and thigh.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: The communal שלמים need waving after שחיטה, and they are waved as they are (whole). These are the words of רבי. The חכמים say: they are waved with the breast and thigh.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic about waving. It brings a ברייתא with a מחלוקת over what part of the communal שלמים is waved after the animals are slaughtered.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everyone agrees there is a waving after שחיטה. The argument is only about what gets waved: רבי says the whole animal, just as it was waved while alive, and חכמים say only the חזה ושוק, like a private שלמים.

keyTerms.meaning: Communal peace offerings, brought on behalf of all of כלל ישראל
Waving of an offering
As they are, the whole animal
The breast and the thigh, the parts of a שלמים given to the כהן

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
The communal peace-offering sacrifices
phrases.notes: These are the two lambs of שבועות, which the משנה already said are waved while still alive.

phrases.english: require waving after slaughter,
and their waving is as they are (whole) —
these are the words of Rabbi.
And the Sages say: with the breast and thigh.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: זִבְחֵי שַׁלְמֵי צִבּוּר טְעוּנִין תְּנוּפָה לְאַחַר שְׁחִיטָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new halachic discussion about waving, after the aggadic side-point.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Communal שלמים are waved after שחיטה. רבי: the whole animal. חכמים: only the חזה ושוק.

steps.title: What is the root of their disagreement?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what principle רבי and חכמים argue about.
steps.simpleTranslation: About what do they disagree?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the reason behind the מחלוקת in the ברייתא. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא wants to find the underlying rule of learning that splits רבי and חכמים, not just know their rulings.

keyTerms.meaning: About what do they disagree? A request for the root of a מחלוקת

phrases.english: About what do they disagree?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind the ברייתא just quoted.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The underlying principle that causes רבי and חכמים to disagree.

steps.title: They argue over how far a learned comparison reaches
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא and רב המנונא answer: the argument is whether we use דון מינה ומינה or דון מינה ואוקי באתרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said to רב המנונא, and some say רב המנונא said to רב חסדא: They disagree about 'learn from it, and from it,' versus 'learn from it, and set it in its own place.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question. The two sides argue over how much we copy when we learn one offering from another.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Communal שלמים learn their waving after שחיטה from private שלמים. With דון מינה ומינה, we copy all the details too, so only the חזה ושוק are waved. With דון מינה ואוקי באתרה, we copy only the basic rule, and the details stay as they are in the communal שלמים' own place, so the whole animal is waved, as it was while alive.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from it, and from it: the learned case takes on all the details of the source
Learn from it, and set it in its place: copy only the basic rule, keep the learned case's own details

steps.whatToRemember: דון מינה ומינה = copy everything from the source. דון מינה ואוקי באתרה = copy only the main rule and keep the rest the way it already is.
steps.whyThisMatters: This pair of rules comes up in many places in ש״ס whenever one case is learned from another.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב חִסְדָּא לְרַב הַמְנוּנָא,
phrases.english: Rav Chisda said to Rav Hamnuna,

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמְרִי לַהּ רַב הַמְנוּנָא לְרַב חִסְדָּא:
phrases.english: and some say Rav Hamnuna said it to Rav Chisda:
About 'learn from it, and from it,'
and 'learn from it, and set it in its place' —
phrases.notes: 'Its place' means the communal שלמים keep their own way of doing things, apart from the one rule being learned.

phrases.english: they disagree.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב חִסְדָּא לְרַב הַמְנוּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 31.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The מחלוקת depends on whether a learned comparison carries over all details (דון מינה ומינה) or only the main rule (דון מינה ואוקי באתרה).

steps.title: How the Rabbis use 'learn from it, and from it'
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן hold דון מינה ומינה: just as private שלמים are waved after שחיטה with the חזה ושוק, so too communal שלמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן hold 'learn from it, and from it.' Just as private שלמים need waving after שחיטה, so too communal שלמים need waving after שחיטה. And 'from it': just as there the waving is with the breast and thigh, so too here it is with the breast and thigh.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now spells out how the רבנן's view comes from the rule of דון מינה ומינה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first 'from it' teaches the basic rule: communal שלמים are waved after שחיטה, like private ones. The second 'from it' carries over the detail too: the waving is only with the חזה ושוק, which is exactly the רבנן's ruling in the ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: Private peace offerings, brought by one person
Just as... so too...: the form used to compare two cases

phrases.english: The Rabbis hold:
'Learn from it, and from it' —
just as private peace-offering sacrifices
require waving after slaughter,
so too communal peace-offering sacrifices
require waving after slaughter.
And 'from it' —
phrases.notes: This is the second 'from it': now we carry over the details too, not just the basic rule.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the principle named in step 32 to the רבנן's side of the ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Using דון מינה ומינה, the רבנן copy both the waving after שחיטה and the detail of waving only the חזה ושוק from private שלמים.

steps.title: רבי copies the main rule but keeps the details local
steps.stepSummary: רבי holds דון מינה ואוקי באתרה. From private שלמים we learn that communal שלמים are waved after שחיטה. But the detail of waving only the חזה ושוק stays with private שלמים, so communal שלמים are waved whole.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי holds: learn from it, but set it back in its own place. Just as private שלמים must be waved after שחיטה, so too communal שלמים must be waved after שחיטה. But set it back in its own place: there, by private שלמים, the waving is done with the breast and thigh. Here, by communal שלמים, the animals are waved as they are, the way they were when alive.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now explains רבי's side of the argument, finishing the explanation started in Step 32. רבי learns the basic rule from private שלמים but not the detail of which parts are waved.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides learn from private שלמים that communal שלמים need waving after שחיטה. The difference is what comes along with it. The חכמים carry over the detail of waving only the חזה ושוק, while רבי says that detail stays with private שלמים, so the communal animals are waved whole.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn the main rule from the source case, but keep the details according to the new case's own setup
Waving: moving the offering back and forth in the בית המקדש
Communal peace offerings: the two lambs brought with the שתי הלחם on שבועות
The breast and thigh, the parts of private שלמים that are waved and given to the כהן
As they are: the whole animal, not cut into parts

steps.whatToRemember: Both רבי and the חכמים agree communal שלמים are waved after שחיטה. They argue only about what is waved: the חכמים say just the חזה ושוק (דון מינה ומינה), and רבי says the whole animal (דון מינה ואוקי באתרה).
steps.confusionAlert: "As they were when alive" does not mean the animal is waved while still alive. רבי agrees the waving here is after שחיטה. It means the animal is waved whole, in the same complete form it had when alive.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows clearly how the two methods of learning one case from another, דון מינה ומינה and דון מינה ואוקי באתרה, can lead to different practical results.
